articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5 in early May 2026, featuring significantly improved long-horizon reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a unified architecture that merges the previous o-series reasoning models with the main GPT line. Benchmarks show substantial gains on PhD-level science questions and complex multi-step coding tasks, with latency improvements over the previous chain-of-thought approach.

articles.title: Google DeepMind Unveils Gemini 2.5 Ultra with 2M-Token Context and Agent Capabilities
articles.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 2.5 Ultra, boasting a 2-million-token context window and built-in agentic tool-use capabilities that allow the model to autonomously browse, write code, and execute multi-step workflows. The model achieves state-of-the-art results on GPQA and SWE-Bench Full, signaling a significant leap in production-ready AI agents.

articles.title: Figure Robotics Begins Commercial Deployment of Figure 03 Humanoid in BMW Factories
articles.summary: Figure announced the start of scaled commercial deployment of its Figure 03 humanoid robot at BMW's Spartanburg manufacturing plant, marking one of the first large-scale uses of general-purpose humanoids in automotive production. The robots handle parts kitting, inspection, and bin picking with a new vision-language-action model that allows rapid task reassignment without reprogramming.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 Demonstrates Autonomous Household Task Completion in Live Demo
articles.summary: Tesla showcased its Optimus Gen 3 humanoid performing unscripted household chores including folding laundry, loading a dishwasher, and navigating cluttered rooms during a live investor event. The robot uses an end-to-end neural network trained on large-scale teleoperation data, a shift from the previous hybrid control stack, and Tesla announced plans for limited external sales in late 2026.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude with Persistent Memory and Long-Running Background Tasks
articles.summary: Anthropic rolled out persistent memory and background task execution for Claude, allowing the assistant to retain user context across sessions and run multi-hour research and coding workflows asynchronously. The feature uses a retrieval-augmented memory architecture with user-controlled privacy settings, positioning it as a step toward always-on AI collaborators for professional workflows.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm-Class N14P Process Node
articles.summary: TSMC confirmed the start of volume production on its N14P (1.4nm-class) process using backside power delivery and gate-all-around transistors, achieving a roughly 15% performance gain and 30% power reduction over N2. Early customers include Apple and NVIDIA, with AI accelerator designs expected to tape out on the node by Q3 2026.

articles.title: Microsoft and Atom Computing Demonstrate Logical Qubit Error Correction Below Threshold
articles.summary: Microsoft and Atom Computing published results showing their neutral-atom quantum computer sustained below-threshold error rates on logical qubits using a topological error-correction code, a milestone toward fault-tolerant quantum computation. The system ran a 24-logical-qubit chemistry simulation that would take classical supercomputers orders of magnitude longer, though commercial viability remains years away.

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces Rubin Ultra GPU Architecture with 576GB HBM4 at Computex Preview
articles.summary: Ahead of Computex 2026, NVIDIA previewed the Rubin Ultra GPU featuring 576GB of HBM4 memory, a new FP4 tensor core architecture optimized for mixture-of-experts inference, and NVLink 6 enabling 3.6 TB/s bisection bandwidth across 72-GPU clusters. The announcement intensifies the AI infrastructure arms race as hyperscalers race to deploy trillion-parameter models at scale.
